races.name: Adare Manor Opportunity Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Timurshah
runners_data.note: Three wins from three starts on Good ground with a fifth on very different ground — the sim-going record (10/11, 3 wins 3 placed) is the standout stat in the field; hold-up style suits this slow-pace scenario perfectly and the 6-day turnaround from a win suggests a horse in form, though 168lbs is a burden in a competitive field.
runners_data.comment: Timurshah arrives on the back of three consecutive wins but our rating of 113 trails his official mark of 122, suggesting he may be flattered by that sequence; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 168 lb is a significant burden to overcome.

runners_data.name: My Trump Card
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old without a win or place on Good going in 14 tries — the sim-going record is the most damning figure here; 100 days off adds further doubt, and Shane Fitzsimons' 4lb claim only partly offsets the concern about ability to handle this surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning after 100 days off, My Trump Card none the less has experience over today's trip and an official mark of 120 to underline his class — the chief concern is a trainer without a winner in 27 attempts over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Tassarolo
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie on, but the five-year-old has never won beyond 13f and all recent runs have been at 12-13f on Good; stepping up significantly in distance is the key question mark, and while trainer Denis Hogan fires runners from low-strike-rate yards the held-up style suits a moderate pace.
runners_data.comment: Tassarolo has won twice and finished second in his last five starts, showing genuine ability, but he carries 164 lb and our rating of 114 leaves him ranked seventh of eighteen — that weight burden looks the chief obstacle after an unplaced effort last time out.

runners_data.name: Teed Up
runners_data.note: Finishes flagged for fading — the form string of 80000 confirms it; the last win on Good came at 17f but that was a rare positive in a sequence of disappointing efforts, and running again just 2 days after a run heightens the concern about freshness.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and back just two days ago, Teed Up nevertheless heads the field on our ratings and has experience of today's distance and going — the question is whether his recent string of unplaced efforts represents a barrier too far.

runners_data.name: Playtime
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's five-year-old has a strong Good-ground profile (9/15 runners finishing) with a win and four places; races held up but can travel prominently, and the 19-day break is sensible — worth respect on pace shape alone even if the jockey booking is moderate.
runners_data.comment: Placed third last time out and a runner-up three starts back, Playtime arrives here in good heart after a 19-day break, with experience over today's trip and going. Yet to win in his last five starts, he carries 163 lb, though his profile makes him our pick at this level.

runners_data.name: Barrys Spirit
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse by nature — though shown in midfield here because of redistribution among a crowded rear group — won at 18f on Good and that win is very relevant; the 246-day absence is the one significant concern, but Adrian Murray has no recent runners to compare against.
runners_data.comment: Landed a win two starts back but has been off the track for 246 days, and that absence is the key question mark; he has run over today's trip and a rating of 114 gives him a fighting chance, though fifth last time out suggests he's not in the most consistent nick.

runners_data.name: Castleheath
runners_data.note: Two career wins — one on Good at 10f, one on Yielding — but the horse has finished tailed off in its only recent run and was absent 216 days; the natural hold-up style is squeezed by redistribution, meaning Eoghan Finegan's 2lb claim must do a lot of work.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and returning from a 216-day absence, Castleheath has plenty to prove here, though he has run over today's trip before and his 113 rating suggests he remains capable at this level.

runners_data.name: Cloonainra
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the race and will lead from the front; form has tailed off badly (9th, 5th, 4th, 8th, 9th in five outings) and the Good-ground record is modest, but the tactical advantage of dictating pace against 17 hold-up types is enormous — McConnell's yard is out of form (0/27 in 14 days).
runners_data.comment: Cloonainra has run over today's trip and going, and her rating of 117 puts her third-best in an 18-runner field — a solid enough case for her landing a blow here. The main risk is a trainer in the depths of a 0-from-27 run, which is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Bannow Blaze
runners_data.note: Won at 16f on Good and placed at 16f on Soft — genuinely useful form — but unseated and fell in the last two runs, raising jumping reliability concerns; a true hold-up type whose redistribution into midfield means Eoin Staples must find clean early air in a big field.
runners_data.comment: Bannow Blaze has a win and a second in recent starts but his last two outings ended in a fall and an unseating, making jumping reliability a real concern; he has experience of today's trip and conditions, though 156 lb is a stiff ask.

runners_data.name: Wahraan
runners_data.note: Won at 18f on Good and placed at 16f on Good — the distance and going profile fits well; only four runs to assess on sim going but a strong record among them, and Carl Millar's 2lb claim is helpful; 4 days since last run is a tight turnaround but the horse showed it can go quick.
runners_data.comment: Wahraan won last time out but was only sixth two starts back, giving him a mixed profile; he has run over today's distance and going, though 154 lb is a stiff burden and four days between runs leaves fitness to prove.

runners_data.name: Mo Ghille Mar
runners_data.note: Three wins at 17f on Good signals the trip and ground suit — but the horse's redistribution out of the deep hold-up group into midfield means Harry Sexton's 4lb claim will need to find clear passage; the 2-day turnaround is a concern and form includes a 13th.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive seventh-place finishes make her hard to fancy, and turning round that form on just two days' rest is a tall ask; she does have experience over today's distance and going, and her win three starts back shows she can find the line.

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: The most consistent horse in the race — five placings from eight recent outings, all on Good, and all at 16-18f; headgear (tongue-tie and pad) suggests the stable is trying to sharpen a horse that keeps getting beaten, but the profile of running second twice at 16f on Good is directly relevant to this race shape.
runners_data.comment: Consistent without converting, Penzance has finished second in three of his last four starts yet remains winless in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going, and 151 lb is a stern test, though his form profile keeps him squarely in contention from the midfield.

runners_data.name: Party President
runners_data.note: Headgear-worn hold-up type whose best recent run was a second on Soft — the Good-ground record is mixed; Dylan O'Connor's 4lb claim and a light weight help, but the redistribution means the horse won't get its most comfortable position in a 18-runner field.
runners_data.comment: Party President arrives just five days after his last start, showing a second four starts back but winless in recent outings and unplaced last time; he has run over today's trip and going, yet ranked 12 of 18 on our rating, he faces a stiff ask here.

runners_data.name: Coolboy Christy
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked 15th of 18 on our figures, Coolboy Christy makes little appeal here despite the fitness of a run just 10 days ago and experience over today's trip and going — the 143 lb burden only adds to his task.

runners_data.name: Imperial Miss
runners_data.note: Returned a strong second at 22f on Good — the longest distance run and a good result — but was absent 231 days and is now running at a shorter trip; the redistribution away from natural hold-up territory compounds an already-difficult ask, and Thomas Gibney's yard has no recent form to encourage.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and absent for 231 days, Imperial Miss faces a stiff ask returning here; ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, she offers little encouragement, though she has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Space Warrior
runners_data.note: Form string includes a 9th, 3rd and 9th at distances shorter than today's — the step up to 2m½f is the appeal, and Thomas Mullins' 1/8 recent strike rate is modest; Sean Cleary-Farrell's 4lb claim helps, but this is a progressive young horse whose redistribution into midfield is manageable.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with a pulled up and a ninth among recent outings, Space Warrior faces a stiff ask ranked 14 of 18 on our figures; he has run over today's trip and going before, and that third two starts back offers a flicker of hope.

runners_data.name: Torque De Lune
runners_data.note: Had a fall and unseated in the last two completed runs — jumping is a live concern at Galway where the fences come fast; the natural style is genuine hold-up but the redistribution flag means Calum Hogan will be hunting ground in a big field, and the 0/1 recent trainer record reduces confidence.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and ranked last on our figures, Torque De Lune has unseated and fallen in her last five — a deeply unconvincing profile; she has run over today's going before, and 16 days between runs at least suggests she arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Dream Shaper
runners_data.note: Won most recently at 19f on Good — the most directly relevant recent form in the entire field for this race shape; tongue-tie on, trainer Madden has just 1 from 2 recently, but the 9-day break after a win and a genuine staying profile on Good make this a horse who could arrive late at a price.
runners_data.comment: Dream Shaper bounced back to win last time out and returns quickly on nine days' rest, with experience of today's trip and going in his favour — but ranked 17 of 18 on our figures, he faces a stiff ask against this field.

races.paceDynamic: Cloonainra is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 18-runner field and, critically, faces no obvious challenger for the lead — she can dictate her own rhythm from the front at a sustainable gallop over 2m½f on Good ground at Galway. With no rival likely to press her hard, the pace will be controlled and moderate through the early stages, which typically compresses the field and sets up a test of jumping accuracy and sustained galloping ability rather than pure finishing speed. The mass of the field — Timurshah, Penzance, Playtime, Dream Shaper and others — are genuine hold-up or midfield types who will be ridden to arrive late, meaning the winner is most likely one who can travel powerfully through the race and produce a clean, sustained run from the home turn. This shape strongly favours hold-up horses with good course form on Good ground who can produce a strong single surge — true closers racing in role — over front-runners trying to steal a march. The field holds far more hold-up/prominent types than the map can accommodate at the rear; Barrys Spirit, Bannow Blaze, Wahraan, Mo Ghille Mar and Penzance are all genuine deep closers who will be competing for ground in the final 2f rather than settling in their natural position early.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cloonainra Controls, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Cloonainra sets a comfortable, uncontested tempo and the hold-up horses get a clean run from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Cloonainra's moderate front-running pace will keep the field bunched, but the sustained nature of the Galway straight on Good ground means those with genuine staying power who travel well will run past her; horses with strong Good-ground hold-up profiles are firmly in their element.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Cloonainra Steals It Wire-to-Wire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slow enough that Cloonainra builds an unassailable advantage turning in and the closers are caught cold.
scenarios.body: With such a large field of hold-up horses, traffic problems and scrimmaging in the straight are real risks, and a clever front-runner dictating can exploit the chaos behind; Cloonainra has Good-ground form and hurdling experience over this sort of trip, and if rivals are stuck in traffic she can slip away.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Fractionally Quicker, Midfield Types Strike
scenarios.trigger: If several of the redistributed hold-up horses push forward earlier than expected and marginally increase the gallop, setting up a true staying test.
scenarios.body: A slightly stronger pace would suit those who travel prominently from midfield and have stamina to sustain it — Penzance has been placed repeatedly at this trip on Good and Wahraan has won at 18f on Good; both can deliver a strong challenge in the final 2f if the race develops more honestly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos and Traffic, Longshot Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the large field causes significant interference in the home straight and the strongly fancied hold-up horses are blocked, allowing a fresher type to slot through.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners on a track that narrows, gaps can close sharply and an unconsidered runner who finds a clean passage could fill a place at long odds; Dream Shaper won recently on Good over this sort of trip and Coolboy Christy has placed form over similar distances.

watchPoints.text: Cloonainra sets the entire race tempo alone — if Patrick O'Brien quickens even fractionally leaving the back, he could build a lead that a field of chaotic hold-up horses cannot close down.

With 18 runners, all predominantly hold-up types by nature, traffic in the home straight is highly probable — watch for Penzance, Wahraan and Mo Ghille Mar getting squeezed for gaps at the critical moment.

Bannow Blaze fell and unseated in consecutive runs — any hesitation or jumping error at the hurdles under a big field rush could cause a fall or unseat affecting nearby runners Castleheath and Torque De Lune.

Timurshah runs just 6 days after a win with 168lbs — if Conor Smithers settles well in the early stages of a moderate pace, this horse's exceptional Good-ground record makes it the defining form reference for the race.

Dream Shaper's recent 19f Good-ground win is directly on point for this trip and surface — at an expected long price, Brian Barry's 4lb claim could deliver value if a clean run emerges in a congested final 2f.

runners_data.name: Burning Ability

runners_data.comment: Landed a win three starts back and was second two starts back, but fifth last time out and returning just a day later is a concern; has run over today's trip and going, though the 164 lb burden makes life harder.

runners_data.name: High Court Cave
runners_data.note: Placed at OR=118 over 22f on Good and won over 18f on Good, so trip and ground are not concerns; amateur Mr O McGill (5lb claim) rides for a trainer who has sent out seven runners over 14 days without a winner, which tempers confidence slightly.
runners_data.comment: Hasn't threatened in his last three starts following a win four starts back, and that form dip is the obvious concern; has experience of today's going, though, and a 35-day break could freshen him.

runners_data.name: Mr Master Mac
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up horse with a perfect sim-going record (5/5 on Good, 2 wins), won at 18f and 19f on Good and his form reads 1-3-1 in his last three completed starts; the 7lb claim of Thomas O'Connor and a 49-day break are the only minor questions in what is otherwise a strong profile.
runners_data.comment: Mr Master Mac won two starts back and has going experience to call on, but seventh last time out is a concern after a 49-day absence, and 163 lb is a stiff burden for a horse ranked eighth of 22.

runners_data.name: Pinot Rouge
runners_data.note: Prominent type whose best recent effort was a 2nd over 24f on Good, but has run on soft or heavy-ground trips in between and his sim-going record is 0 wins from 15 similar runs; headgear (hood or pads noted) and a 50-day break add uncertainty.
runners_data.comment: Placed second last time out and third three starts back, Pinot Rouge shaped with plenty of promise in recent outings, and our rating of 126 — highest of the 22 runners — marks her as a serious contender; the main concern is 50 days off the track.

runners_data.name: Rocky's Howya
runners_data.note: The principal front-runner, with two wins from five attempts on Good including a win over 24f at Galway; the tongue-tie is noted and trainer-jockey combination of Declan and Mr D L Queally (amateur) is an obvious stable confidence signal.
runners_data.comment: Rocky's Howya has won three of his last five starts, including a victory last time out, but a pulled-up run four starts back raises a fitness question; he has experience of today's distance and going, though 162 lb is a stern test.

runners_data.name: Fou De Toi
runners_data.note: Paul Townend takes the ride for Mullins, whose yard is in exceptional form (10/47 over 14 days); Fou De Toi's sole sim-going run produced a second place over 20f on Good, though just one Good-ground data point is a limitation.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts and ranked 16 of 22 on our figures, Fou De Toi faces a stiff task carrying 161 lb; the pulled-up run two starts back is a concern, though he has shown placing ability and has run over today's going before.

runners_data.name: Reiki Revolution
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been struggling for form (P4-UU4) and carries a tongue-tie and hood; sim-going record shows a reasonable 11th-of-14 median but the recent run of unfinished or unseated efforts on softer ground is concerning even on a better surface.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts — including two unseats — and with his trainer yet to land a winner in 30 attempts over the past fortnight, Reiki Revolution faces plenty to prove at 161 lb, despite having run over today's trip and going before.

runners_data.name: Stormbreaker
runners_data.note: Hold-up type who placed second over 19f on soft and ran well fresh, but the rest of his recent form has been on soft or heavy ground — his only Good run recently saw him miss the finish; the 21-day return and mediocre sim-going figures make him hard to trust.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time is the obvious concern, but Stormbreaker showed clear ability with a second five starts back and has going experience to call on; winless in his last five, he returns after 21 days carrying 161 lb with a rating of 124 giving him plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Warriors Wood
runners_data.note: Very consistent hold-up performer, three wins and six placings from 13 sim-going runs, all on Good, and last four runs include a win and two places over 20-22f at Galway; the 7lb claim of Kevin Healy and a 2-day turnaround are minor concerns against strong credentials.
runners_data.comment: Warriors Wood shaped with real promise when third three starts back and winning four starts back, and he handles today's going — but that eighth last time out, on just two days' rest, is the one concern.

runners_data.name: Elusive Ogie
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has run 11 times on Good-going trips and has a win and three places to show for it, though his recent form includes a fall and two moderate efforts; form reads 5-9-0-5 in most recent starts, suggesting he needs things to fall right.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Elusive Ogie at least has experience of today's going and returns on a reasonable freshness of 16 days; the 159 lb burden, however, looks a stiff ask for a gelding ranked ninth of 22.

runners_data.name: Moonovercloon
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with a visor on and a modest sim-going record (13th of 15 median); form of 0-P in last two starts and a 2-day turnaround for the Queally yard make him hard to recommend with confidence.

runners_data.name: Forceonmyown
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott runner making a 110-day return to action for a yard with 4 wins from 42 in the last 14 days; his sim-going record offers no wins from 8 Good-ground runs, and the absence is a significant handicap at this trip.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, with a best recent effort of third four starts back, Forceonmyown faces a stiff ask off 153 lb after a 110-day absence — though our rating of 111 suggests she retains more ability than her recent form implies.

runners_data.name: Tullyveery Lad
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a strong sim-going pedigree — 15 of 15 runs on Good ground with 2 wins and 6 placings — and was second over 24f on Good last time; the breast-plate noted and 27-day break are non-issues, making him a durable each-way option in most pace shapes.
runners_data.comment: Tullyveery Lad has placed twice in his last five starts — second last time out and third five starts back — but has three unplaced efforts in between and remains winless in recent starts; he has run over today's trip and going before, though his ranking of 12th of 22 suggests he faces a stiff task.

runners_data.name: Mento
runners_data.note: The second confirmed front-runner, a 4-year-old who won over 19f on Good penultimate start; his youth and limited experience over 3m½f are genuine question marks, and if he gets into a battle with Rocky's Howya from the off his stamina may be tested well before the finish.

runners_data.name: Beggars Rock
runners_data.note: Hold-up type whose best sim-going run was a 3rd over 26f on Good; tongue-tie noted and 78-day absence is a concern, though the 11-of-15 median on Good shows he handles the surface — just not enough class to be confident in a field this competitive.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Beggars Rock does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and a third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement — but 78 days off the track and a 148 lb burden make this a tough ask from 11th in the rankings.

races.paceDynamic: Rocky's Howya and Mento are the two confirmed front-runners in a 23-runner field, and both have recent evidence of leading and winning — Rocky's Howya has won three of his last five starts including a front-running success over 2m4f at Galway, while Mento led and won over 19f on his penultimate start. With two genuine pace-setters going head-to-head over an extended 3m½f trip on Good ground, the race will be run at an honest, possibly pressured gallop from the outset, which stretches the field and burns off horses who have to work hard to hold their position. The field holds more prominent and hold-up types than can all secure their natural positions — Burning Ability, High Court Cave, Pinot Rouge and Elusive Ogie are genuine prominent horses most likely to secure the front rank behind the two leaders, while Wild Mandate, Sallap, Justatan, Fair Damsel and Pat Coyne are pushed into a midfield mapping that does not reflect their true style. A genuinely contested pace over this stamina-sapping trip strongly favours resolute, proven stayers who can race with cover in midfield and produce a sustained gallop from the home turn — pure hold-up horses who get the race truly run to suit are the primary beneficiaries, provided they are genuine in their role and not redistributed types.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Stayers Prevail
scenarios.trigger: If Rocky's Howya and Mento fight it out up front and set a strong honest gallop that stretches the field over the final mile.
scenarios.body: The two leaders burn each other up and the race becomes a true test of stamina from three out, with the pace blunting the chance of any horse who had to work hard to hold a prominent position; genuine stayers racing in rear-midfield with cover get a rhythm and come through powerfully.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one pace-setter, most likely Rocky's Howya, edges Mento out early and controls the gallop at a measured tempo from the front.
scenarios.body: Rocky's Howya has won three of his last five and has proven front-running ability at Galway specifically; if he settles into a rhythm without being truly pressured he can husband his stamina reserves and make the jumping count over the final obstacles.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves steady enough that the prominent trio of Burning Ability, High Court Cave and Elusive Ogie can sit close without exerting themselves through the early stages.
scenarios.body: A moderate gallop means those racing just off the pace do not get emptied and arrive at the last two flights with stamina intact and a positional advantage; prominent-style horses with good form on Good ground are the direct beneficiaries in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Fail to Materialise
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses — Sallap, Justatan and Fair Damsel — are drawn wide or shuffled back further than ideal and cannot find clear daylight in a large 23-runner field.
scenarios.body: Racing out of role in a big field over extreme distances tends to produce messy passages and blocked runs, making this shape the least reliable; the style-fit penalties on these runners correctly temper expectations and the probability is accordingly low.

watchPoints.text: Rocky's Howya and Mento are on a collision course for the early lead — if Mento's young legs take the battle to Rocky's Howya from the first hurdle, both could be empty turning for home and the entire front-running scenario collapses in favour of rear-midfield closers.

Warriors Wood has three wins from 13 Good-ground runs and a 2-day turnaround; connections running him back so quickly at Galway suggests they are very live about his chance — watch for him to be produced with a well-timed run from the back of midfield.

Mr Master Mac has a perfect sim-going record (5/5) and is a hold-up type ridden by a 7lb claimer — in a big field of 23 he will need a clean passage from three out, and if he gets trapped on the inside rail behind tiring horses his run may arrive too late.

runners_data.name: Soldante
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with strong Good-ground form (3 places from 3 runs on Good), 6 days since last run keeps him fresh, apprentice Eoghan Finegan claims 5lb and the 169lb burden is notable, but sitting just off the pace is his natural game here.
runners_data.comment: Soldante showed a win two starts back but has otherwise been placed or just outside — consistent without being dominant. Has experience on today's going and ran just six days ago, so freshness may be a question carrying 169 lb.

runners_data.name: Ira Hayes
runners_data.note: Won over 22f on Good and placed twice at the trip, 56 days between runs is worth monitoring, hood fitted and Michael Kenneally claims 5lb; if fit he travels prominently and this distance suits his stamina profile well.
runners_data.comment: Ira Hayes arrives with solid recent form — a winner three starts back and second two starts back — and has experience of today's trip and conditions, carrying 168 lb; the concern is his trainer's barren run of 0/27 in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Journey So Far
runners_data.note: Holds a win over 22f on Good but the form note flags a tendency to fade in the finish — a significant red flag over 2m6½f with a genuine pace; Keith Donoghue rides and 65 days off adds doubt about sharpness.
runners_data.comment: Winning last time out gives Journey So Far a live chance, but 65 days off the track and a trainer without a winner in 30 recent attempts are significant concerns; he has run over today's trip and going before, though a hefty 168 lb burden further complicates matters.

runners_data.name: Kings Jet
runners_data.note: Natural hold-up horse with one win on Good at 23f, pulled up or unseated on three of five starts suggests jumping reliability is a concern; amateur Mr Halford claims 7lb but the erratic record makes him hard to trust at this level with 18 rivals.
runners_data.comment: Kings Jet arrives with strong recent form — a win and a second in his last five starts — and has experience of today's trip and going, while 30 days since his last run suggests he comes here fresh; the concern is two consecutive non-completions heading into this.

runners_data.name: Lawful Ruler
runners_data.note: One of the confirmed front-runners, won over 24f on Good and clearly loves to dominate from the front; with Gorthill also pressing, he will need to handle a contested early pace, and his last run ended in a pull-up which queries current form.
runners_data.comment: Pulled up last time and ranked 16 of 18 on our figures, Lawful Ruler is hard to fancy at the weights despite a win three starts back; experience on today's going is the one genuine plus.

runners_data.name: Sammy Smart
runners_data.note: Veteran ten-year-old who has placed three times in his last five on Good, sits in behind the pace and grinds; James Smith claims 5lb but the form shows no win in 18 runs on Good — honest rather than dangerous.

runners_data.name: Golden Temple
runners_data.note: Ran just 4 days ago for Noel Meade — very short turnaround that needs watching, tongue-tie fitted; recent form is strong including a Good-ground win at 20f, and Sam Ewing gives him a professional rider at this level.
runners_data.comment: Golden Temple showed good recent form with a win two starts back and followed up with a second last time out, but he carries a hefty 163 lb and that burden, combined with a run just four days ago, makes recovery a key question here.

runners_data.name: Prince Palace
runners_data.note: Struggling for form — no win or place on Good in 15 attempts and five outings show a string of modest finishes; blinkered, held up, and the course/going record makes it hard to find a compelling angle.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and carrying a hefty 162 lb, Prince Palace nonetheless boasts experience over today's trip and going, and our rating of 114 marks him as a serious player — though a patchy recent record, including two pulled-up efforts, is the obvious concern.

runners_data.name: Inchidaly Copper
runners_data.note: Exceptional Going record — 14 of 15 runs on Good with four wins, most recently third at 20f; amateur Luke Burke Ott claims 7lb and the consistent prominent style suits this pace shape strongly, making him a key player.
runners_data.comment: Ranked near the foot of our figures and carrying 161 lb, Inchidaly Copper faces a stiff ask, though he has experience over today's trip and going, and a win in his last five starts shows he can find the line.

runners_data.name: Le Grand Vert
runners_data.note: Won over 25f on Good and has placed in that band before, 21 days between runs is fine; ten-year-old veteran who races prominently, but the recent form string shows two pulls-up from five, which tempers confidence.
runners_data.comment: Le Grand Vert has pulled up in two of his last five starts and, ranked 15th of 18 on our figures, is hard to fancy here; however, he has winning form and distance-and-going experience in his favour, and 21 days gives him a fair freshener.

runners_data.name: Drop A Threat
runners_data.note: Mullins-trained and lightly raced, T14 form of 10/47 shows the yard is firing in the current spell; genuine hold-up horse by inclination who has struggled on Good in recent outings — needs gaps to open late in a big field, which Galway rarely provides.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Drop A Threat was sixth last time out and fifth two starts back, with a pulled-up run three starts back a concern; he has run over today's trip and going, but 160 lb is a stiff ask as he seeks a change of fortune.

runners_data.name: Noble Talent
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old with a string of pulls-up and poor finishes; a true hold-up horse who is mapped into midfield by congestion — his chance is compromised by having to race forward of his natural position, and the STYLE_FIT score of 0.93 reflects that risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in recent starts and pulled up in three of his last five, Noble Talent arrives 57 days fresh carrying 159 lb; he has run over today's trip and going, but that patchy record makes him hard to trust despite a rating of 112 suggesting more ability than he's shown.

runners_data.name: Riggs
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old veteran, has run on Good every time in the last 15 starts with two wins and three places — experience counts; a genuine hold-up horse pushed into midfield by the field's overall shape, so his natural late run may be harder to deliver here.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and twice pulled up in that sequence, Riggs faces a stiff ask off 159 lb, though he has run over today's distance and going before and returns after a 33-day break with some fitness in reserve.

runners_data.name: Jukebox Johnny
runners_data.note: Recent second on Good over 22f is the standout recent piece of form, 73 days off is a gap to note; De Bromhead handler sends him for a prominent pitch and the tongue-tie/pad combination suggests he needs to be ridden up with the pace to be seen to best effect.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out but winless in his last five starts, and 73 days off the track is a fitness query; Jukebox Johnny has run over today's trip and going, yet a hefty 158 lb burden and a ranking of 12th of 18 suggest he faces a stiff task here.

runners_data.name: Gorthill
runners_data.note: The second confirmed pace-setter, has placed twice in staying chases on Good and shown front-running tendencies; ten-year-old who has had four consecutive disappointing runs including two pulls-up — stamina may be the issue if he tries to force the pace over 2m6½f.
runners_data.comment: Gorthill has run over today's trip and going before, and our rating puts him narrowly ahead of this field — yet his recent form, including two pull-ups and an unseating in his last five starts, gives some cause for pause at 156 lb after 72 days off.

runners_data.name: Saunton Surf
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 24f and placed in that range twice more, 50 days off is acceptable and the pace (p) headgear suggests he wants to be handy; form figures of 1-2 in the last two are the best in-running sequence in this field.
runners_data.comment: Won her most recent run after a runner-up effort and, before that, two fifths and a pulled-up run, Saunton Surf bounces back after 50 days off carrying 156 lb and ranked 13 of 18 on our figures — distance and going experience offer some hope, but she's hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Smallcraftwarning
runners_data.note: Six placings from 14 Good-ground runs but no wins; a true hold-up horse forced into midfield by the redistribution, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 racing out of role makes his task harder — tongue-tie fitted for John Patrick Ryan.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 14th of 18 on our figures, Smallcraftwarning looks hard to fancy carrying 156 lb; a second three starts back offers a slim crumb of comfort, and he has run over today's distance and going before.

runners_data.name: Mistyburn
runners_data.note: Won on Good at 24f, young six-year-old still developing, tongue-tie and pad fitted; a hold-up horse by nature who is mapped forward into midfield by field size — his chance depends on a pace collapse, which is possible but not the dominant scenario.
runners_data.comment: Consecutive sixth-place finishes make Mistyburn hard to fancy — ranked last on our figures and carrying 143 lb, the handicapper offers little encouragement. He has winning form in recent starts and handles today's going, but he needs a sharper effort than his latest two outings suggest.

races.paceDynamic: Lawful Ruler and Gorthill are the confirmed pace-setters in an 18-runner field, and with both committed front-runners in the gate the early gallop will be genuine rather than dawdled — over 2m6½f on Good turf at Galway that creates a true-run test from the outset. The fractions will be honest enough to compress the field early but the distance is stamina-sapping, meaning the front two are unlikely to both last home and the race will be won by whoever handles the transition from mid-race cruise to the final-circuit grind most efficiently. Prominent racers who can sit a length or two off the pace and save their energy — Soldante, Ira Hayes, Inchidaly Copper, Saunton Surf and Jukebox Johnny — are best placed to strike in the straight without needing a sustained challenge from deep. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their natural position: Riggs, Noble Talent, Smallcraftwarning and Mistyburn are genuine hold-up horses mapped into midfield because the pace congestion pushes them forward of their ideal spot, and they are less likely to thread through 18 runners late on Good ground at Galway; the tactical verdict is clear — prominent racers who travel economically just off a contested lead hold the structural advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Lawful Ruler and Gorthill set a genuine pace and the prominent brigade track them efficiently through the middle mile.
scenarios.body: The contested early gallop burns off the leaders inside the final circuit, leaving the horses who sat just off the pace with the clearest run and the most fuel; the stamina test on Good Galway ground rewards horses that stayed out of trouble at the front without making all.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfielders Swoop
scenarios.trigger: If the front runners go too hard early and blow up before the last, allowing midfield runners to pick up the pieces.
scenarios.body: Lawful Ruler and Gorthill push each other along faster than the distance demands, leaving them spent before the final climb, and the midfield pack — some of whom are naturally prominent but dropped back by the congestion — emerge with running.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Lasts Home
scenarios.trigger: If one of the pace-setters — most likely Lawful Ruler — is allowed to control the pace alone after the other fails to hold their position.
scenarios.body: With 18 runners creating early crowding, Gorthill or Lawful Ruler could find themselves running at their own rhythm if the chasing pack gets tangled; Lawful Ruler has won at this trip on Good ground and could prove hard to reel in if the fractions remain manageable.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Closers Late Burst
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly fierce and the entire prominent-to-midfield pack tires, opening a gap for deep hold-up types to finish strongly.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape because the horses mapped at the rear — Riggs, Noble Talent, Smallcraftwarning, Mistyburn — are redistributed away from their true home and will not find the gaps a genuine hold-up horse would at Galway's testing finish; Drop A Threat from the Mullins yard is the only credible closer with the class to thread through.

watchPoints.text: Inchidaly Copper holds the best Going record in the race — 14 of 15 starts on Good with four wins and consistent prominent style — watch him as the primary danger to the pace-stalkers once Lawful Ruler and Gorthill are consumed.

Golden Temple ran just 4 days ago for Noel Meade; the extremely short turnaround on a stamina test of 2m6½f is a fitness-vs-freshness concern, and if he ties up after a quick return he could cause interference in the closing stages of a big field.

Lawful Ruler's last run ended in a pull-up, and if his jumping or stamina gives way mid-race while leading a 18-runner field the resulting scramble at fences poses risk for several horses immediately behind him.

Saunton Surf arrives with the best recent form sequence in the field (1-2 in last two on Good), 50 days off and pace headgear fitted — watch his market move and early positioning as a possible dark horse for the prominent shape.

Drop A Threat carries the most powerful trainer profile (Mullins, 10 winners from 47 in the T14 window) but is a true hold-up horse in a race where hold-up types face a structural disadvantage — watch for whether Danny Mullins adapts his ride or accepts a deep position.

races.name: Lord Hemphill Memorial Handicap Steeplechase

runners_data.name: Blood Destiny
runners_data.note: OR 150 front-runner partnered by Paul Townend for Mullins (10/47 14-day strike), 62 days fresh, Good-ground form solid (sim-going 7/15, 1W4P) — the class act in the race and a confirmed leader who must be caught if allowed any daylight.|
runners_data.comment: Blood Destiny arrives here second last time out and a winner four starts back, with previous experience of today's distance and going and a rating of 156 that puts him clear of his rivals. The 62-day absence is the one query, but his profile makes him the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Coming Up Easy
runners_data.note: Henry De Bromhead runner (5/39 14-day) returning after 114 days off, but three wins on Good over comparable trips give confidence; sits naturally prominent and has the stamina to grind through a contested gallop, making him the most dangerous tracking presence in the field.|
runners_data.comment: Two wins in his last four starts, including back-to-back victories, show Coming Up Easy in good heart, and he has experience of today's distance and going; a return from 114 days off is the one question to answer.

runners_data.name: Runcok
runners_data.note: A genuine front-runner at OR 133 who has to share pace duties with a higher-rated rival today — finished down the field last two on Good, sim-going 8/11 only 1W1P; if the duel costs him, he may fade approaching the last.|
runners_data.comment: Runcok has run over today's trip and going, and his win four starts back shows he can compete at this level, but three runs without troubling the judge since, a 69-day absence, and a trainer who is winless in 27 recent attempts all work against him under 149 lb.

runners_data.name: Le Nez Creux
runners_data.note: Lightly raced five-year-old for Cromwell with Mark Walsh aboard, all five recent runs at prominent style on Heavy — the step to Good and this trip (2m2f) is new territory, but the form figures (13152) are smart and the profile is promising if conditions suit.|
runners_data.comment: A winner three starts back and second last time out, Le Nez Creux arrives with solid recent form and has the profile to make her presence felt off a 132 rating; the chief concern is a trainer running cold at 0/30 over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Path d'Oroux
runners_data.note: Ran only yesterday (LR: 1d) which is a serious fitness concern regardless of form; hold-up type on evidence (sim-going 8/15, 0W2P) whose last five Good-ground runs have yielded nothing better than third, and the turnaround makes engagement here puzzling.|
runners_data.comment: Rated 140 and ranked second of 12, Path d'Oroux holds strong claims on his official mark of 130, and has run over today's trip and going; the chief concern is a trainer without a winner in 30 attempts over the past fortnight, and he arrives just one day after his last outing.

runners_data.name: The Banger Doyle
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran hold-up type with fine course form (2/17f/GOO, 3/16f/GOO), suited by Good and this distance range, but 0W7P in sim going tells its own story — needs everything to go perfectly and rivals to tire.|
runners_data.comment: Yet to score in his last five starts, The Banger Doyle at least showed ability when second last time out, and has run over today's trip and going before; carrying 145 lb against higher-ranked rivals, however, makes progression hard to envisage.

runners_data.name: Drumgill
runners_data.note: Hold-up rider from the John Patrick Ryan yard, sim-going record 7/15 with 0W0P — has the stamina base from a step down in trip but has yet to convert on Good ground and a 5lb claimer (Kenneally) is an uncertain commodity in a competitive handicap.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and pulling up two runs back are real concerns, but Drumgill has run over today's trip and going before and bounced back to finish fourth last time out; a rating of 130 gives him something to work with from the middle of the field.

runners_data.name: Lisleigh Lad
runners_data.note: Genuinely prominent-raced type who won over 20f on Good last time out; OR 123 gives a weight edge and the horse's sim-going record (12/15, 3W6P) is excellent — one of the most naturally suited runners to the expected race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Ranked bottom of the field on our figures, Lisleigh Lad faces a stiff ask off 140 lb, and his last-five form — a winner last time out but fourth and third in the starts before that — is inconsistent; experience over today's trip and going at least removes one unknown.

runners_data.name: War Correspondent
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has placed four times in last five on Good ground (sim-going 14/15, 1W6P) — consistent without winning, ran just seven days ago, and the 5lb claimer Paddy Hanlon adds risk, but the trip and going suit.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, with an unseating thrown in, War Correspondent is hard to fancy ranked 11 of 12 on our figures; he does return quickly on familiar distance and going, and a third last time out offers a crumb of encouragement.

runners_data.name: Itsalladream
runners_data.note: Consistent Good-ground performer (sim-going 13/15, 2W4P) whose natural style is to race from the rear — with more hold-up types than rear positions available, this horse is pushed forward on the map but will likely be further back than ideal, tempering its chance of getting a clear run.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Itsalladream has nonetheless been running consistently in the minors, and he has experience of today's trip and conditions; the 140 lb burden may be the biggest obstacle to bridging that gap.

runners_data.name: Watch The Weather
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old whose best form includes a win on Good (sim-going 12/15, 1W3P), but inclined to race from behind; the redistribution forward on the map reflects field congestion, not a change in riding tactics — a 5lb claimer on a genuine backmarker adds further positional risk.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked ninth of 12 on our figures, Watch The Weather is hard to fancy at 140 lb; a second three starts back offers a crumb of hope, and experience over today's trip and going at least removes any unknown.

runners_data.name: Bythesametoken
runners_data.note: Aged twelve, returning after 114 days, with a recent form figure of 9th on Good — natural hold-up style that is compressed into a midfield map slot by field dynamics rather than by intent, and the combination of age, layoff, and style mismatch makes this a tough assignment.|

races.paceDynamic: Blood Destiny and Runcok are confirmed front-runners who will clash for the lead from the off, creating a genuinely contested gallop over 2m2f on good ground at Galway — neither is the type to yield and Paul Townend on the higher-rated Blood Destiny (OR 150) will likely dictate terms if Slevin on Runcok cannot match strides early. This contested pace scenario should produce an honest, relentless gallop that tests stamina into the finish rather than building to a single kick, favouring prominent riders who can track closely without burning fuel in the duel and closers who stay on at one pace rather than sprinting. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Itsalladream, Watch The Weather, and Bythesametoken are genuine backmarkers redistributed into the midfield positions, meaning the horses most likely to actually secure prominent tracking spots are Coming Up Easy, Le Nez Creux, and Lisleigh Lad. In this shape — a truly run race over a stiff test — prominent trackers with proven Good-ground form and clean jumping hold the tactical edge over the pure hold-up brigade, who will likely be further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny and Runcok trade blows from the front and set an honest gallop that softens both before the last, allowing a prominent tracker to sweep past.
scenarios.body: The two pacemakers drain each other, and the horse sitting third or fourth without being in the scrap arrives fresher at the business end over the stiff Galway finish; Coming Up Easy and Le Nez Creux have the profile, both proven on Good and capable of producing a jump at the last.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Blood Destiny shakes off Runcok early — perhaps after a jumping error from Runcok — and is allowed to dictate a controlled pace from the front.
scenarios.body: With Paul Townend masterclass-managing the tempo from the front, Blood Destiny (OR 150, 7 Good-ground runs) can conserve enough to quicken clear approaching the last and hold on; at this distance on Good he has the class advantage and jumping profile to make all under a seasoned pilot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the front two empty inside the final half-mile and a midfield type delivered late picks up the pieces across the flat run-in.
scenarios.body: Lisleigh Lad has the most genuine stamina evidence at this trip on Good ground with a recent course win and could motor home; War Correspondent's consistent placing record (four times in the money last five) suits a staying-on scenario from a tracking position.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: True Hold-Ups Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough and long enough to bring the genuine backmarkers into the picture despite their redistributed map positions.
scenarios.body: This scenario is materially discounted because Itsalladream, Watch The Weather, and Bythesametoken are all operating out of their natural rearward positions in a field this deep, reducing the clean ground and late kick they need; even in a true strong-pace meltdown, the Galway run-in is short enough to blunt the advantage of a late rush from a compromised position.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Runcok attempts to match Blood Destiny stride for stride from the start — if Slevin pushes hard for the early lead, the pace could become genuinely scorching and leave both front-runners vulnerable from three out.

Path d'Oroux ran only yesterday; monitor in the betting market and paddock for any signs of distress or withdrawal — a horse running on back-to-back days at this level is a significant welfare and performance flag.
Le Nez Creux has never run on going better than Heavy in its last five starts — if the Good ground rides quick, watch for any signs of it not handling the surface during the first mile.

Coming Up Easy is returning from 114 days off for De Bromhead — watch for market support as a confidence indicator that the yard is happy with the preparation, given the yard's 5/39 14-day strike rate suggests horses are ready when they run.

The cluster of hold-up horses (Itsalladream, Watch The Weather, Bythesametoken) will be fighting for the same rear ground — watch the early-race positioning to see whether any of them push forward unexpectedly, which could alter the pace calculation significantly.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Ahonoora Handicap

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Prominent-travelling type who has won over 8f on Good ground twice recently — dropping back to 7f at Galway could sharpen his finishing kick, and Jack Kearney's 3lb claim is useful; only 5 days since his last run but clearly in a good moment of form.
runners_data.comment: Jagged Edge was third last time out and a winner three starts back, showing he retains the ability to hit the frame; he has run over today's trip and going, and at just five days since his last start, freshness could be a minor query, though a rating of 105 suggests he has the class to go well from stall 14.

runners_data.name: Vafortino
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up horse who has been well below his best across 10 recent Good-ground starts with zero wins; 45 days off may have freshened him but the style and record on this going make him hard to be optimistic about.
runners_data.comment: Vafortino heads this field on our ratings and has run over today's trip and going, bringing relevant experience to the table from stall three at 138 lb — though his recent string of finishes outside the places makes a first win a pressing concern.

runners_data.name: Dorset
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the entire pace dynamic for this race; A P O'Brien's string has been firing (6/52 in 14 days) and Lordan's association gives him every chance, but the form line of 78940 reads like a horse that needs things to fall right, and front-running in a handicap of this size carries risk.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Dorset nonetheless rates 108 on our figures — second of 17 — and has experience of today's trip and conditions; the risk is that an unplaced effort just four days ago raises freshness concerns.

runners_data.name: Dunum
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old prominent racer who ran third over this course and distance in soft last year — the upgrade to Good is a minor concern — and his form has been inconsistent, but he races prominently and will be in the right part of the field throughout.
runners_data.comment: Dunum has experience over today's distance and going, and his win four starts back shows he can find the winning thread — a rating of 106 underlines he has the class to threaten. The worry is consecutive unplaced efforts in his last two runs.

runners_data.name: Gleneagle Bay
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who won over 7f on Good at this track (1/7f/GOO in recent history) and that course-and-distance win stands out; the blinkers applied suggest connections want him travelling more keenly, and DBM riding is a significant plus in a race where a clear run matters.
runners_data.comment: Gleneagle Bay won two starts back but has been sixth last time out, and five days between runs is a quick turnaround; he has run over today's distance and going before, though carrying 134 lb from stall 17 adds to the task.

runners_data.name: Orandi
runners_data.note: An honest sort who actually wants to race from the rear but has been pushed into a midfield mapping here due to the surplus of hold-up horses — his best form (sim-going 7/15, one win on Good) has come when getting a clear run late, and racing closer than ideal may not suit.
runners_data.comment: Orandi won last time out but that victory came just five days ago, and he carries 134 lb from stall 18 having looked inconsistent in his two runs prior; has run over today's trip and going, though his patchy recent record gives pause.

runners_data.name: Unique Journey
runners_data.note: Has been running at 6f mostly but steps up to 7f here; the two wins in the form string came at 6f on Good or Yielding, and whether he gets home on this longer trip in a big field is a genuine query — prominent style means he will not be short of room.
runners_data.comment: Boasts back-to-back wins in recent starts, though he's been unplaced last time out and hasn't run in 71 days; has experience of today's trip and going, but that return from absence is the key question from stall 11 off 134 lb.

runners_data.name: Lord Massusus
runners_data.note: Consistent sort who has placed third at 7f on Soft recently but records zero wins or places on Good ground across 10 runs — that record is a structural concern and he will need things to change materially to factor.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Lord Massusus does at least bring distance and going experience to the table, and our rating of 102 suggests he retains ability — but a latest unplaced effort and third five starts back represent the key extremes of a frustratingly inconsistent profile.

runners_data.name: Bold Style
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse but ends up slotted into midfield on this map given the volume of closers in the race — his Good-ground form shows three places at 8f and he has dropped back to 7f; Andrew Slattery training and riding his own horse.

runners_data.name: City House
runners_data.note: Prefers to come from well off the pace but with so many true hold-up types competing for that ground, he is effectively forced to run from mid-division; Adrian McGuinness has been in decent form (2/28 in 14 days) and his 4/7f/GOO and 5/6f/GOO recently show he is not out of form.
runners_data.comment: Yet to win in his last six starts, City House nonetheless brings distance and going experience to the table, and 15 days since his last run suggests he arrives fresh; the 130 lb burden and a draw of 15 are the notable counterweights at a mark of 92.

runners_data.name: Dark Ace
runners_data.note: Strong recent form with two 6f wins on Standard and places at 5f and 6f on Good, but this 7f trip on turf Good looks beyond his optimum — primarily a sprint type who holds up and needs a fast pace over a shorter trip to show his best.
runners_data.comment: An unplaced latest run after a pair of thirds makes Dark Ace hard to fancy ranked 13 of 17 on our figures, and 130 lb is a stiff burden from stall 16; he has run over today's trip and going before, and two wins in his last five starts show he retains ability.

runners_data.name: Far From Dandy
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who has been consistent at 8f on Good but has finished no better than second in those efforts and holds a headgear marker (p); stepping down to 7f should theoretically sharpen the finish but his trajectory is one of coming up short.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, Far From Dandy does offer two seconds in recent form, though back-to-back unplaced efforts are a concern; has run over today's trip and going, and 130 lb from stall five makes life no easier.

runners_data.name: Dos Mukasan
runners_data.note: True hold-up type whose best form (win and place) came on Standard surface at Southwell, not on Good turf; 91 days off is a concern and he finds himself mapped to midfield because the rear is overcrowded — his real chance depends on conditions he is unlikely to get here.
runners_data.comment: Three consecutive unplaced efforts make Dos Mukasan hard to fancy, and he arrives 91 days fresh; a win four starts back offers slim encouragement, and he has run over today's trip, but our figures rank him last of the field.

runners_data.name: Pierre Royal

runners_data.comment: Pierre Royal won two starts back and was second last time out, so he arrives in form, but five days is a quick turnaround and 129 lb is a stiff burden; he has run over today's trip and going before, though ranked tenth of seventeen on our ratings.

runners_data.name: Genuine Article

runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and returning on a quick five-day turnaround, Genuine Article faces a stiff ask, though he has run over today's distance and going before and a rating of 96 gives him some theoretical upside from stall 10 off 125 lb.

runners_data.name: Lir Speciale
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent type who has placed in five of his last 15 Good-ground starts and hit the frame at 7f (2/7f/GOO, 4/7f/GOO) recently; Chris Hayes rides and this horse will be sitting in exactly the right place to challenge if Dorset's lead crumbles.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts and ranked 15th of 17 on our figures, Lir Speciale faces a stiff task, with his trainer yet to strike in 29 attempts over the past fortnight; he has run over today's trip and going before, and stall one is his lot off 87.

runners_data.name: Greydreambeliever
runners_data.note: Placed twice at 7f on Good recently and Joseph Patrick O'Brien's yard is firing at 15/78 in 14 days — however, he is a natural hold-up horse redistributed to midfield here, meaning he races closer than ideal; the strong form line makes him one to respect despite the positional compromise.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked 14th of 17 on our figures, Greydreambeliever arrives just three days after her latest fourth, making the quick turnaround a concern; a second three starts back offers mild encouragement, but the overall profile is hard to fancy.

runners_data.name: Glory To Be
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on Good and placed at 6f and 7f multiple times — the Good-ground 7f profile is right and this prominent racer ridden without a jockey name (no claim noted) has the positional profile to benefit if the pace gets hot and Dorset weakens.
runners_data.comment: Beaten out of the sights last time after back-to-back placed efforts, Glory To Be heads into this rated below her official mark and ranked near the foot of the field on our figures — hard to fancy despite having experience of today's trip and conditions.

races.paceDynamic: Dorset is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead in an 18-runner 7f handicap at Galway, Wayne Lordan can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front without being pressed. The pace will be honest rather than blistering — Dorset's recent form shows a horse that settles in front rather than scorching clear — meaning the race shapes as a processional lead with a measured mid-race tempo that sets up a strong late drive from the home turn. Prominent racers such as Jagged Edge, Pierre Royal and Lir Speciale will travel in the slipstream and be best positioned to pick off a tiring Dorset if the pace eases, while genuine hold-up horses such as Gleneagle Bay and Lord Massusus will need a strong enough pace to generate the late surge their style demands. This race shape firmly favours prominent-to-mid-division types who travel well behind the leader and can produce a sustained run from two furlongs out, rather than true closers who rely on a contested gallop to drag them into contention. Several horses tagged as redistributed — City House, Bold Style, Dos Mukasan and Genuine Article — are genuine hold-up types who cannot secure their natural rear position; of the redistributed group, City House and Bold Style are most likely to actually sit closer than usual given their tactical versatility.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dorset Leads, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset controls the pace unchallenged and the prominent horses travel smoothly behind before delivering sustained runs from two out.
scenarios.body: Lordan sets a measured fractions on the front end, leaving the prominent chasers sitting comfortably before unleashing their challenge entering the final furlong; horses who travel kindly just off the pace have all the momentum at the business end.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Arrive
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset's lead becomes too comfortable and the gallop slackens enough in the middle of the race to allow true hold-up horses to close with a single sweeping run.
scenarios.body: A slow mid-section compresses the field, and horses that were tracking from midfield get a clear run to use their sustained finishing pace in the final furlong; Gleneagle Bay and Lord Massusus, genuine hold-up types who made it to their natural positions, are the principal beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Dorset accelerates sharply off the home turn and a genuine test of stamina over the Galway 7f emerges.
scenarios.body: A strong fractions-to-finish race eliminates horses who are over the top at the furlong pole and rewards those with proven stamina at this trip on Good ground; horses like Lir Speciale and Pierre Royal, with solid 7f form on this ground, keep finding as rivals fade.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Breaks Out Wide
scenarios.trigger: If the large 18-runner field creates positional trouble and horses get shuffled back or blocked in the straight, handing an advantage to those drawn wide or ridden patiently with a clear passage.
scenarios.body: Traffic problems compromise several prominent-midfield runners and the winner emerges from an unexpected position, rewarding horses with the tactical profile to sidestep trouble and finish with a clear run.

watchPoints.text: Pierre Royal has run just five days ago, returns to Good ground where he has a 2W4P record from six starts, and travels prominently for the in-form McGuinness yard — watch him as the horse whose profile fits this race shape most precisely.

Gleneagle Bay won over this course and distance on Good and Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride — a horse with a proven Galway 7f win who is fitted with blinkers and is a genuine hold-up type who made it to his natural position, making him the main danger if the pace is even slightly strong.

Dorset's ability to front-run without pressure in a field of 18 could produce an unusually slow mid-section — if Lordan gets a soft lead and slows it down between the 5f and 3f marks, the race could compress into a sprint that catches prominent horses flat-footed and launches the genuine closers.

Multiple redistributed hold-up horses (Bold Style, City House, Dos Mukasan, Genuine Article, Greydreambeliever) will be racing closer than their natural style dictates — watch for early scrambling in the first two furlongs as these horses try to settle in an unfamiliar position, which could create traffic issues behind the leader.

Dark Ace's best form has come at 5-6f on Standard surfaces — the step up to 7f on Good turf is a material concern and bettors should note that his recent win-form flatters a sprint profile that may not translate here.

runners_data.name: Hypiradon

runners_data.name: Miss Cornelia
runners_data.note: Gary Carroll rides this lightly-raced unknown quantity for Joseph Murphy who has managed just 1/7 over 14 days; a single 6th-place debut run over 7f good gives little to go on, though the trip is proven and good ground is fine.|

runners_data.name: Gabby Hayes
runners_data.note: Noel Meade debutant with no form to assess and going unknown — connections have form with lightly-raced types at Galway, and Siobhan Rutledge on board suits the conditional rider angle; completely unexposed so must be respected as a wild card despite the absence of evidence.|

runners_data.name: Oristown Boy

runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes the ride for Joseph O'Brien, whose barn has been in excellent form at 15/78 over 14 days; two placed runs from four starts all came on good ground over 7f, making this the standout profile for the dominant scenario — held-up horses wearing headgear (p) noted.|

runners_data.name: Star Glory
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for Noel Meade ridden by Chris Hayes; recorded a placed run over this exact trip on good and is effectively guaranteed the lead, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) means that if the race turns into a sprint finish the advantage of dictating may be lost — more danger-horse than banker.|

runners_data.name: Someday Somewhere
runners_data.note: W J Lee rides this lightly-raced type for Stephen Thorne who has had no winners from 10 runners over the last 14 days; one placing from a single debut run over 6f on good shows some promise, and the step to 7f for a horse with style unknown leaves the profile genuinely open.|

races.paceDynamic: Star Glory is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival likely to push them hard from the gates, sets up to dictate a sustainable, uncontested gallop over Galway's 7f on good ground. Dakota Jack and Seaxburh are the two prominent types capable of tracking closely, but neither is a habitual leader who will force Star Glory into a pace battle. Hypiradon is a true hold-up type redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is already occupied by Scotty Cameron, Oristown Boy, and Whosinterviewinwho — meaning those closers face a genuinely congested finish battle off a moderate tempo. With one horse able to control tempo throughout and no credible challenger for the lead, this race shape strongly favours runners who can sit prominently behind Star Glory and strike in the final two furlongs, as the absence of a pace duel limits the advantage of hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to reel the front rank in.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Star Glory bowls along unchallenged and sets a fair, even gallop that suits a prominent stalker to pounce late.
scenarios.body: Star Glory's uncontested lead produces a well-judged pace that blunts the hold-up brigade while setting up the final quarter-mile for those sitting second or third; Seaxburh and Dakota Jack, tracking closely, are ideally placed to kick past a potentially tiring leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Quicken Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Star Glory is caught and passed by a prominent rival in the final furlong as the pace is just strong enough to string the field out.
scenarios.body: The steady fractions mean that a prominent tracker with latent pace can sweep past a Star Glory who has briefly gone to the well too early; Seaxburh's two placed efforts at this trip on good ground make her the prime beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Strongly
scenarios.trigger: If Star Glory's pace is fast enough to set up a proper finish, allowing the hold-up brigade to close ground through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Scotty Cameron, Oristown Boy, or Whosinterviewinwho would need the leader to have gone quick enough to burn themselves and the prominent trackers out; this is the least natural shape given how moderate the pace is likely to be with no rivals forcing Star Glory's hand.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Maiden Chaos Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If a slow start, crowding, or a false-pace collapse reshuffles the field and produces a bunch finish with no clear tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: In a race full of inexperienced two-year-olds, a messy start or mid-race surge could bunch the field into the final furlong where an unexposed horse like Gabby Hayes or Miss Cornelia lands a windfall; form lines count for little in a true scramble and raw ability surfaces.

watchPoints.text: Star Glory's uncontested lead is the race's pivot — watch whether Chris Hayes sets a truly controlled pace or allows the gallop to drift slow enough that the field bunches dangerously in the final furlong.

Seaxburh (Dylan Browne McMonagle/O'Brien) must be tracked from the stalls — if she secures a prominent berth tracking Star Glory, her two placed runs at this exact trip and going make her the most pattern-fit horse in the race.

Hypiradon is mapped further forward than its natural position warrants; if Rory Cleary is forced wide or into an uncomfortable slot mid-race, the horse's already-limited form chance is compromised further.

Gabby Hayes is an O'Brien-rivalling Noel Meade debutant with zero form lines — monitor how it settles early; an unexposed horse in a maiden with weak form at the top can land races like this without warning.

The cluster of hold-up types (Scotty Cameron, Oristown Boy, Whosinterviewinwho) will likely be racing from well off the pace — watch whether they find any cover or are forced wide on the turn, as either position kills their already-slim late-pace hopes.

races.name: Village Salthill Handicap

runners_data.name: Iamimmaculate

runners_data.name: Mr Ballynonty

runners_data.name: Blue Blue Moon

runners_data.name: Felix Somary
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with a visor, last seen finishing third over 10f on Good — encouraging but flagged as fading in finishes, which is a significant concern in a genuinely-run race at this trip; trainer John O'Donoghue hits 1 from 3 over the last 14 days.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out and carrying a workable weight of 132 lb from stall four, Felix Somary has run over today's trip and going and our rating suggests he's better than his official mark of 72 — yet he remains winless in his last five starts, and that lack of a win is the concern.

runners_data.name: Snow Princess

runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Snow Princess nonetheless showed genuine promise with a third two starts back and returns here on a snappy eight-day turnaround, with experience of today's trip and going in her favour; the risk is she has yet to translate that ability into a win.

runners_data.name: Good Man Jack
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who raced just 2 days ago and carries a fade-in-finish flag; form string of 0-9-7-8 does not inspire confidence and the quick turnaround adds risk in a competitive 13-runner handicap.

runners_data.name: Tharaka
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for the Emmet Mullins yard, which returns 2 wins from 17 in the last 14 days; ran only 2 days ago but has placed twice over Good ground in recent starts, and the trip looks well-suited — best placed of the genuine hold-up contingent to secure a handy midfield berth given tactical versatility.

runners_data.name: Aquilla Star

runners_data.name: Unfamiliar
